messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: prod-ratecap-ops fired at 1978888888 - high 429 spike detected on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. alert: 14% error-rate over 3m. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/ratecap
pagerduty: Incident triggered -> prod-ratecap-ops. Notified: Alex C (primary), Raj P (secondary)
Alex C: acked. I'm on it. Can someone paste recent deploys/config changes to ratecap?
Raj P: I pushed a config tweak ~28m ago: quota-mapper v2.3.1, enabled feature-flag `strict-tenant-map`.
Maria S: running a quick check on limiter pods now
Maria S: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=ratecap -o wide`
Maria S: pod-1 CrashLoopBackOff, logs show repeated "quota not found -> default 0" for many tenant ids
Raj P: that explains the 429s — quota-mapper returning 0 means ratecap thinks tenants have no quota.
Taylor G: can we flip the feature-flag to permissive? I can push a configmap hotfix. Permissive mapping should restore prior behavior while we debug.
Alex C: do it. we'll need to scale replicas too while rolling. keep me posted.
Taylor G: applying `permissive-mapper.yaml` now (turn off strict-tenant-map).
incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for configmap/quota-mapper-permissive at 1978888898
Maria S: scaling ratecap deployment to 5 replicas while config rolls `kubectl scale deploy ratecap --replicas=5 -n prod`
pagerduty: Alex C acknowledged the incident at 1978888895
SupportBot: Notifying #sre-support and on-call AEs for potential customer impact
Kim H: joining the thread, will take handoff in ~10m if needed
Raj P: after config flip: 429s dropped from 14% -> ~2% within 60s for most tenants. Nice.
Alex C: good. any tenants still impacted?
Maria S: two enterprise tenants (enterprise-123, enterprise-77) still showing elevated 429s. digging into tenant->quota mappings. logs show tenant-id != quota-key for some requests.
Raj P: suspect cache rehydration bug: when quota-mapper restarted with strict flag on, some cache entries expired/rehydrated incorrectly, producing missing keys and zero quotas.
Taylor G: I'm rolling back the mapper image to v2.3.0 as a precaution to restore known-good behavior: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/quota-mapper -n prod`
incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for deployment/quota-mapper at 1978888928
Maria S: monitoring per-tenant 429 rate: enterprise-123 dropped from 18% -> 1.5% after rollback, enterprise-77 similar improvement.
Alex C: notify AEs for those accounts and tell them mitigation is applied. @SupportBot can you post the templated customer note?
SupportBot: Posted to #support-ops and queued outbound email to AE list: "We observed transient throttling affecting a subset of tenants due to a quota-mapping regression. Mitigation applied and service stabilized. Follow-up with timeline and root cause to follow."
Kim H: taking over incident ownership at 1978889000 (handoff). Alex, anything to add?
Alex C: thanks. I'm starting the incident timeline doc and will add notes. Kim owns the remainder of monitoring and PD updates. Raj/Taylor please own root cause and fix.
pagerduty: PD: escalated to SRE-leads as a standard follow-up; status -> acknowledged -> monitoring
Taylor G: root cause hypothesis: cache-rehydration + strict mapping flag. Action items I'm opening now: enforce non-zero default fallback, startup validation that checks quotas for active tenants, add metric `quota_mapper.startup_validated` and alert if missing_quota_count>0 on boot.
Raj P: opened PR #458 for startup validation and guardrail. adding tests for cache TTL alignment.
Maria S: per-tenant telemetry shows 95% of traffic back to normal. keeping additional replica while we monitor.
Alex C: timeline notes for postmortem: incident start 1978888888, permissive flip 1978888902, rollback 1978888928, handoff 1978889000, stabilized ~1978889080. PM: Raj P (primary), Taylor G (secondary).
Kim H: putting incident in monitoring state, will wait 30m of stable telemetry before closing. Notifying Customer Success for proactive outreach.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=monitoring, severity=SEV3, customer-impact=partial_throttle, runbook_ref=https://confluence.redwood/incidents/ratecap-ops
Alex C: thanks team. postmortem in 48h, include remediation and deployment gating for feature flags.
